rv.q: I’d say strain every nerve and sinew to bag a ticket to the funniest double-act stage comedy since the Right Size’s early Noughties tribute to Morecambe and Wise, The Play What I Wrote.
With real freshness and agile ingenuity, the pair up the ante on the perception that a comedy double act is a metaphor for the gains and losses of codependency.
This play about comedy double acts – or is it a comedy routine about theatre? – by Radio 4 gag-merchants The Pin , aka Ben Ashenden and Alex Owen, is the perfect pre-Christmas present.
That’s a crying shame: this backstage farce by double act The Pin is great fun, and will be even more so when Alex Owen, Ben Ashenden and their helpers bed in to its particular haywire rhythms.
The Comeback, crisply directed by Emily Burns, has the duo’s habitual quizzicalness and agility but with slapstick as well as puns, and a plot that tips its hat to stage glories.

The show, which has been developed and expanded in the two years since it was a runaway hit at the Edinburgh Fringe, is built around a clever notion: a lowly double act are providing a warm-up act on a comeback tour by a traditional variety duo, Jimmy and Sid. Ashenden and Owen play both teams.
Their punchlines are all subverted expectations and deliberate anti-climaxes, wryly satisfying but too arch and insubstantial to ever earn a belly laugh.
When, not if, that happens, she has a hugely welcome, heartwarming hit on her hands.
Whichever it is, The Comeback is hugely enjoyable.

For all its smartness, it has at its centre a sweetness and an innocent enjoyment of comedy for comedy's own sake that feels the perfect antidote to the complicated world we are living in, a vaccine against cynicism.
There’s delightful fun here, including a running gag about the way props seem to get smaller when you take them on stage and a neat exploitation of a guest celebrity.
This sweet if slight 90-minute evening of comedy is itself a place-filler intended to keep the Noel Coward warm until its longer-term tenant, Dear Evan Hansen, can itself start up again.

The Comeback allows two immensely talented, up-and-coming actors to talk live on stage about the charms, eccentricities, and general fun of their industry – all the while telling a genuinely hilarious and engaging stage play.
The comedy pair, directed by Emily Burns, have adopted some great material and written some exciting new material themselves, but at times the execution is somewhat lacklustre.
Fun, brilliantly executed and a celebration of the art of performance, it's exactly the kind of entertainment that is needed at this time.

cn.t: Critics find this meta-theatrical farce from comedy duo The Pin hugely enjoyable and very funny, praising its surreal silliness and affectionate homage to double acts, though some note the sketch-based humor proves uneven.
